notes: San Francisco Municipal Reports (SFPL scans on the Internet Archive): the annual reports of the City Architect (from 1912 the Bureau of Architecture) to the Board of Public Works, fiscal years 1907-08 to 1912-13 - every school, firehouse, police station, hospital and civic building the city designed or let contracts for after the 1906 fire, with locations, architects, contractors, costs and completion dates. Locations of schools come from the Superintendent of Schools' property lists and of firehouses from the Fire Department company rosters in the same volumes.

coverage.remaining: The 1913-14 to 1916-17 volumes (munisanfrancisco63-66sanfrich) have no City Architect narrative; their bond-issue building tables are column-scrambled in the OCR and were not read. The FY1905-07 volume (sanfranciscomuni56sanfrich) has no City Architect report. The pre-1906 volumes (1859-1905) are unread.
coverage.note: Read whole: the City Architect reports in sanfranciscomuni57 (pp. 736-747), 58 (pp. 565-571), 59 (pp. 606-640), 60 (pp. 919-927), 61 (pp. 1077-1087) and munisanfrancisco62 (pp. 579-582). Skipped on purpose: the 1908 survey of the ruined City Hall (pp. 743-760 of vol. 57; the building is gone and its site is the Civic Center), temporary buildings, repair and yard-work contracts, the Board of Health and Isolation Hospital repairs, and the playground field houses.

citation.label: San Francisco Municipal Reports for the fiscal year 1909-10, Report of City Architect, p. 632

raw.text: INGLESIDE POLICE STATION — R. R. AVE. AND OCEAN AVE. ... General — E. W. Elliot $38,936 ... completed on July 29, 1910.

resolution.method: The record states no street number, so there is nothing to look up in sf-eas-addresses.
resolution.note: The record locates it only as "INGLESIDE POLICE STATION — R. R. AVE. AND OCEAN AVE.". Kept so the record is not read again; per the evidence bar in research/AGENTS.md it cannot become a page.

findings.address_as_written: RICHMOND POLICE STATION (6th Avenue, near California Street).
findings.description: The Richmond Police Station, two brick buildings for the station and its stable on the west side of Sixth Avenue near California Street, was occupied by the police department; Robert Trost built it on a $32,397 general contract.

citation.label: San Francisco Municipal Reports for the fiscal year 1911-12, Report of City Architect, p. 1083

raw.text: RICHMOND POLICE STATION (6th Avenue, near California Street). Two class "C" brick structures comprising station and stable building. Occupied by Police Department December 25, 1911. ... General Dec. 8, 1911 Robert Trost 32,397.00

resolution.method: The west side of Sixth Avenue near California carries the police-station parcel (block 1538 lot 7, 461 6th Ave and 450 7th Ave), the Richmond station today.

findings.address_as_written: POTRERO POLICE STATION (20th and Kentucky Sts.)
findings.description: Robert Trost took the $21,272 general contract for the Potrero Police Station: a station and a stable for fifteen horses, of concrete and brick finished in white cement plaster, with Oregon pine inside, separated by a wide court.

citation.label: San Francisco Municipal Reports for the fiscal year 1911-12, Report of City Architect, p. 1079

raw.text: POTRERO POLICE STATION (20th and Kentucky Sts.) ... General Aug. 16, 1911 Robert Trost 21,272.00 ... The exterior walls are of concrete and brick finished with a white cement plaster. The interior finish throughout is of selected Oregon pine ... accomodations for fifteen horses

resolution.method: The report gives the southwest corner of 20th and Kentucky (Kentucky is Third Street today); the police-station parcel there is the existing 2300 3rd St page.

findings.address_as_written: ENGINE HOUSE, NO. 28, (Stockton, near Greenwich).
findings.description: O. C. Holt took the $23,940 general contract for a new firehouse for Engine Company No. 28, brick with a pressed-brick front on granite bases, built for four pieces of motor apparatus, with gasoline tanks under the sidewalk and quarters for a battalion chief upstairs.

citation.label: San Francisco Municipal Reports for the fiscal year 1911-12, Report of City Architect, p. 1079

raw.text: ENGINE HOUSE, NO. 28, (Stockton, near Greenwich). ... General May 17, 1912 O. C. Holt $ 23,940.00 ... The exterior walls are of brick, the front being laid up in pressed brick with granite bases ... will accommodate four pieces of automobile fire apparatus

resolution.method: Stockton near Greenwich: the fire-station parcel there is 1814 Stockton, Engine 28's house, the existing page.

findings.address_as_written: CITY HALL (Van Ness avenue, Polk, Grove and McAllister streets).
findings.description: The first contracts for the new City Hall were let: excavation to the Contra Costa Construction Co. on March 19, 1913 ($23,950), and the structural steel to the U.S. Steel Products Co. on June 18 ($476,283).

citation.label: San Francisco Municipal Reports for the fiscal year 1912-13, Bureau of Architecture, p. 581

raw.text: CITY HALL (Van Ness avenue, Polk, Grove and McAllister streets). Excavation, March 19, 1913, 'Contra Costa Construction Co $ 23,950.00 Structural Steel, June 18, 1913, U. S. Steel Products Co 476,283.00

resolution.method: The two blocks between McAllister, Grove, Van Ness and Polk are the City Hall parcel, the existing page.
